title: Nike Slides on Job Cuts; Broadcom Gathers AI Chip Funding | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Nike (NKE) shares continue their slide as it is cutting jobs and overhauling its business as results deteriorate, with a restructuring plan to save $2.5 billion over the next five years. The company expects a high-single-digit revenue decline this year, which is worse than the 2.4% drop projected by analysts, and shares of Nike fell as much as 9.7% in New York on Friday.
- Broadcom (AVGO) shares are moving on news the company's Wall Street syndicate are starting to gather $60 billion of fresh AI chip financing to benefit Anthropic and other companies.
- Fair Isaac Corp. (FICO) shares are rising after the company launched the FICO Mortgage Direct License Program, and Bill Pulte signaled he wasn't purposefully targeting the company, which may have contributed to the stock's rise on Thursday. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tesla Sales Top Estimates for Third Quarter
summary: Elon Musk's Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter topping the estimate of 463,761. Sales are still down from a year ago. Bloomberg's Craig Trudell reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Amazon’s Smart Glasses Raise Privacy Fears
summary: Amazon is equipping its delivery drivers with smart glasses that capture images of their surroundings. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Dave Lee explains how this raises questions about privacy, data use and the future of delivery work. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Further Targets Iran-Linked Russian A7 Financial Network
summary: The US imposed a new round of sanctions on Russia’s A7, a financial services firm accused of using a global network of shell companies to move funds for sanctioned businesses, including in Iran.

title: Chey Tae-won Sells $700 Million in SK Shares During High-Profile Divorce
summary: Chey Tae-won, the billionaire behind memory chipmaker SK Hynix Inc., is selling 944 billion won ($700 million) worth of shares in the conglomerate SK Inc., amid what is set to be among South Korea’s most expensive divorces.

title: Onsemi Revises the Terms of Synaptics Deal
summary: Chipmaker Onsemi revised the purchase terms of its acquisition of Synaptics, agreeing to pay about $5.7 billion in cash rather than roughly $7 billion in shares. Carmen Reinicke reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nvidia Hits First Record Since May as Value Nears $6 Trillion
summary: Nvidia Corp. shares hit a record for the first time since May as investors pile back into the stock after a two-month selloff that wiped more than $1 trillion off its market value.

title: Blackstone, Banks Gather $60 Billon for Broadcom AI Chip Deal
summary: Broadcom’s Wall Street syndicate is starting to gather $60 billion of fresh AI chip financing to benefit Anthropic PBC and other companies, according to people with knowledge of the matter. Carmen Reinicke has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Roblox’s (RBLX) Newest Bear Says Wall Street Is Too Optimistic On Recovery
summary: A recent rally in shares of Roblox Corp. has gone too far and signals investors are overly optimistic about a potential recovery in bookings growth, according to the stock’s newest bear.

title: Lockheed CEO Maps Pivot to Move at `Skunk Works' Speed
summary: Lockheed Martin Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jim Taiclet wants all of the world's largest defense contractor to move nimbly and innovate like the company's secretive Skunk Works unit. He speaks with Bloomberg Television's Ed Ludlow. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Lockheed’s ‘Big Bet’ Tests CEO Plan to Move at Skunk Works Speed
summary: Outside Washington DC in mid-September, Lockheed Martin Corp. lifted the tarp on a futuristic stealth drone: all sleek edges, mysterious vents and not a single pane of glass.

title: Microsoft, Amazon Cloud Arms Set to Face Deeper Scrutiny Under EU’s Tech Rules
summary: Microsoft Corp.’s Azure and Amazon Web Services are set to be designated under the European Union’s strict rulebook for Big Tech.

title: Paramount Backer Cardinale Says CEO David Ellison Is the ‘Future’ of Hollywood
summary: The founder of RedBird Capital says the merger with Warner Bros. will be positive for the industry

title: Amazon’s Latest Response to AI Data Center Backlash: $1 Billion
summary: Amazon.com Inc.’s latest attempt to address the intensifying blowback to an unprecedented buildout of computing infrastructure: a commitment to spend more than $1 billion over the next five years on initiatives for the communities near its server farms.

title: AI Talent Race Between US and China Is the Next Battleground
summary: China and India account for the bulk of international grad students in the US — and increasingly they’re headed home.

title: NYC’s AI Office Boom Is Bust for Young Job Hunters, Report Finds
summary: New York’s artificial-intelligence boom is drawing massive investments and fueling a surge in office leasing, but it’s doing little for young workers trying to start their careers, according to a report by the Partnership for New York City.

title: Nidec Is in Talks With MUFG Bank, SMBC to Renew Credit Lines
summary: Nidec Corp. is in talks with MUFG Bank Ltd. and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. to renew committed credit lines that currently total ¥600 billion ($3.8 billion), the company said on Thursday.

title: CMA Says Nexfibre’s Alt-Net Deal Could Hurt Competition
summary: Nexfibre Networks Ltd.’s £2 billion ($2.7 billion) deal for rival Netomnia Ltd. could reduce competition in the UK’s wholesale broadband networks, the country’s competition watchdog said on Friday, potentially threatening the first major consolidation in the crowded fiber market.

title: SoftBank Stock Investors See Past Credit Risks to AI Returns
summary: SoftBank Group Corp.’s equity investors are increasingly focused on the potential returns from its AI bets, helping the stock rebound even as the Japanese company faces higher borrowing costs.

title: Nvidia Faces Questions Over China AI Chip Smuggling Cases
summary: The company’s AI chips keep making their way to China despite US curbs. Officials are asking why the company missed red flags.
